title: Guarantee terminal crediting on midstream client aborts and reconnects
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Streaming requests that are aborted by clients (network drop, client process crash, user cancellation) sometimes leave the billing pipeline without a definitive terminal event. This causes two classes of issues: (1) under-crediting where output tokens produced but not flushed to the metering store are never charged, and (2) double-crediting when resumed/replayed fragments are later reconciled and both original partial and resumed fragments are counted. The problem is exacerbated by midstream model switches and routing fallbacks where the runtime may produce output under a different model variant mid-request.

Goal: Ensure deterministic, auditable, and idempotent terminal crediting for streaming sessions so that final token counts are correct and explainable regardless of client aborts, reconnections, partial retries, or midstream model switches. The solution should maintain low-latency streaming behavior and not add pathologically high overhead to hot code paths.
acceptance_criteria:
1) For every streaming session id (session_id) we emit exactly one final 'session_finalized' metering record within the reconciliation window (24h) that summarizes input tokens, output tokens, model variants used, and credit attribution.
2) If a client reconnects and resumes the stream with the same idempotency token within the TTL, the final metering record must not double-count previously credited fragments.
3) If a client reconnects with a different session id but includes the server-provided last-ack checksum, we detect overlap and attribute only uncharged tokens.
4) Midstream model switches produce segment-level model attribution in the final record (e.g., model:v1:100 tokens, model:v1-quant:50 tokens).
5) Edge tests (network drop, duplicate writes, partial flush) pass in CI and a canary showing zero revenue delta vs. canonical ground-truth for 1000 synthetic sessions.
6) Observability: create dashboards for orphaned-streams, double-credit-detection-rate, and session_finalized latency.
implementation_plan:
1) Introduce a lightweight session tombstone state stored in the metering store: (session_id, last_ack_token_idx, last_output_checksum, finalized=false, model_segments:[]). Use compact append-only records to avoid hot row updates.
2) On each fragment flush, write idempotent fragment records with (session_id, fragment_seq, fragment_checksum, output_token_count, model_tag). These must be idempotent upserts keyed by (session_id, fragment_seq).
3) When a terminal condition is observed (client close, server-side timeout, heartbeat TTL expiry), run a finalize step that compacts fragments into a single session_finalized record and atomically flips finalized=true via a single conditional write. The finalization computes de-duplicated token counts and model-segment attribution.
4) For reconnects: if a resume occurs with same session_id, resume will re-use fragment_seq numbering and upserts will be no-ops for already-seen seqs. If reconnect uses a new session_id but includes last-ack checksum, run overlap-diff logic during finalization.
5) Add model-seg tags when runtime does midstream model switch; every fragment records the active model_tag for that fragment. Finalization merges contiguous segments for reporting.
6) Implement optimization: keep in-memory per-node pending fragment cache with opportunistic flush to reduce storage pressure; also allow a fast-finalize path for sub-second closed sessions to avoid background compaction.
7) Extend existing reconciliation job to merge late fragments into pending tombstones and to re-run finalization for sessions closed without a finalizer.
8) Provide a read-only API for customer-facing invoices to fetch session_finalized records and the fragment audit trail.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for idempotent fragment upserts and conditional finalize write semantics.
- Integration tests: simulate network drop at N different points (before first flush, between flushes, after model switch) and validate finalization result equals ground-truth.
- Fuzz tests: generate randomized fragment duplication and out-of-order delivery; confirm final deduplicated token counts.
- Load test: run 10k concurrent short streams with simulated reconnects to validate latency impact and storage throughput.
- Billing sandbox run: route 1% of production traffic through a shadowed finalizer that writes to a separate billing index and compare aggregated revenue over 48h.
- Canary: deploy to staging, then prod-canary region with metrics thresholds for rollback (orphaned_streams > 0.1% OR double_credit_rate > 0.01%).
monitoring_and_rollout:
- Create dashboards: 'orphaned_streams', 'double_credit_rate', 'finalization_latency', 'fragment_upsert_errors'.
- Alerts: P1 if double_credit_rate > 0.05% over 15m, P1 if orphaned_streams growth rate spikes.
- Rollout plan: behind feature flag. Phase 1: internal shadow finalizer on 100% of traffic (no writes to billing index) for 48h. Phase 2: canary writes to billing index for 1% of traffic for 72h. Phase 3: ramp to 25% then 100% with monitoring gates.
- Backout: disable finalizer commit and fall back to old aggregator (maintain both paths during canary).
- Postmortem window: collect and hold all session_finalized audit trails for 30 days for dispute resolution.
notes_and_history:
2026-03-10: Ticket created by Asha after customer support flagged two billing disputes where customers were either undercharged or charged twice after client-side cancels.
2026-03-11: Spike investigation by Liam and Noor: reproduced double-count locally by simulating reconnect with new session_id + overlapping checksum. Root cause: fragment upserts allowed duplicate fragment_seq across session boundary when resume semantics were ambiguous.
2026-03-12: Design session tombstone + conditional finalize chosen in sync design review. Trade-offs: small storage amplification for per-fragment records vs. correctness and auditability.
2026-03-13: PR #1234 opened (runtime changes) and PR #1240 for billing worker. Early integration tests show finalization latency median 12ms for small sessions and 280ms p95 under load.
Next steps: finish integration tests, implement customer-facing read API, and schedule canary per rollout plan.
